title: Audit event schema v2: add event_id + category taxonomy (compat mapping)
author: Marcus Lin
description:
Context: As part of SIEM-ready audit export beta (ENG-5127), downstream delivery is at-least-once and we need stable dedup keys plus a consistent category taxonomy for filtering + mapping into Splunk/Datadog. This PR updates core audit event emission to include: (1) `event_id` (stable unique id per event) (2) `schema_version: 2` and canonical `category` / `subcategory` / `action` fields (3) a compatibility mapping layer so existing producers that still emit legacy `event_type`/`operation` continue to work while we progressively migrate call sites.

Summary of changes: Add `event_id` generated at emission time using UUIDv7 (time-ordered, collision-safe) and plumbed through the AuditEvent struct. Introduce an enum-backed category taxonomy with a small canonical set and a `category_version` constant to make future taxonomy evolution explicit. Add a `legacy_event_type` field (optional) and a mapping table from legacy strings to v2 taxonomy, used for any call site still emitting legacy types. Update JSON serialization + redaction hooks so `event_id` is always present and never redacted, while category fields are required and validated. Add golden fixtures + unit tests to lock schema output. No changes to retention/storage semantics in this PR.

Taxonomy (v2, initial): categories = {authn, authz, workspace, api_key, model, deployment, billing, data_access, security, system}. `subcategory` is optional but recommended for high-volume categories (e.g., `api_key.rotation`, `authz.role`, `deployment.route`). `action` remains a verb phrase in present tense (create/update/delete/rotate/enable/disable/login/logout/impersonate/etc) and is required.

Compatibility: Existing events that provide `event_type` will have `legacy_event_type` set, and the mapping table populates `category/subcategory/action`. If mapping is missing, we default to `category=system`, `subcategory=audit.unknown_legacy_type`, `action=emit` and include a structured warning log (rate-limited) so we can clean up unmapped call sites before GA.

Follow-ups: (a) migrate remaining emitters to pass v2 taxonomy explicitly, removing reliance on legacy mapping (b) update docs + examples in security/compliance Confluence (c) exporter service uses `event_id` for idempotency keys (separate PR).

Testing: unit tests for UUIDv7 generation + monotonicity (best-effort), mapping table tests (known legacy types), JSON golden files for representative events, and a redaction regression test to ensure `event_id/category/action` survive redaction.

Rollout: behind `AUDIT_SCHEMA_V2_ENABLED` (default ON in dev/staging, OFF in prod until exporter beta gate is ready). When flag is OFF, we still emit legacy fields only and omit v2 additions.

Risk: Low-medium. Primary risk is unexpected unmapped legacy event types causing `system/audit.unknown_legacy_type` categorization; mitigated via logs + metrics + follow-up cleanup.
commits: audit: add event_id to AuditEvent + propagate through emit()
audit: introduce category taxonomy types + validation
audit: legacy event_type -> v2 mapping table (initial set)
audit: add JSON golden fixtures + schema regression tests
audit: gate v2 fields behind AUDIT_SCHEMA_V2_ENABLED flag
telemetry: add counter for unknown_legacy_type + rate-limited warning
checks: CI: build (pass), unit-test (pass), lint (pass), typecheck (pass), security-scan (pass). Initial run failed on lint due to fixture filenames; fixed in follow-up commit and re-ran successfully.
conversation:
Kevin Osei (review): Can you clarify the id generation strategy and whether downstream should treat `event_id` as globally unique across tenants? Also please confirm we are not putting any extra PII in the new fields.

Marcus Lin (author): Using UUIDv7 generated at emission time; uniqueness is global (across all tenants) and safe to treat as a dedup key. No PII added: event_id is random/time-ordered, category/subcategory/action are controlled vocab/verbs only. No IP/user agent changes in this PR.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): +1 on adding the v2 fields, but I’d like validation behavior spelled out. What happens if an emitter passes an invalid category? Also, please ensure RBAC-sensitive events don’t end up in a generic bucket without visibility.

Marcus Lin (author): Added validation: invalid category/subcategory/action causes emission to fail closed in dev/staging (throws) and fail open in prod (drops v2 fields, emits legacy + increments `audit_schema_v2_validation_failed_total`). For generic bucket: when legacy mapping missing we emit `system/audit.unknown_legacy_type` AND a metric + warning log so we can track it.

Ethan Park (review): Flag default worries me. We need predictable behavior for exporter (it will assume event_id exists). Suggest: v2 flag ON everywhere but keep legacy fields for now; or make exporter gate separate.

Marcus Lin (author): Adjusted per your suggestion: `event_id` is always emitted when v2 flag is ON; prod default remains OFF until exporter readiness, but we’ll enable both together via the tenant allowlist flag. Added a TODO in ENG-5127 checklist and updated the flag description to reflect coupling.

Logan Wright (review): Please add a metric for unknown legacy mapping and include the legacy value as a *low-cardinality* label (or not at all). We don’t want cardinality explosions.

Marcus Lin (author): Added `audit_unknown_legacy_type_total` with labels `{service, env}` only. The legacy string is logged (rate-limited) but not a metric label.

Benji Okafor (review): Golden fixture tests look good. One nit: `subcategory` format should be consistent (dot-separated). Some fixtures use underscore.

Marcus Lin (author): Fixed fixtures + added a test enforcing `^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9]+)*$` for subcategory when present.

Approvals: Kevin Osei (approved), Kaitlyn Nguyen (approved), Ethan Park (approved), Logan Wright (approved).

Merge: Squashed and merged after CI green.
release_notes: Audit logs (schema v2, gated): add `event_id` and canonical category taxonomy to support SIEM export filtering + downstream deduplication.
